author: Noah Jeffries STAFF WRITER
title: Stockert Youth Center receives $13K donation for playground upgrades, opens registration for basketball program | Buckhannon News - Breaking and more | wvnews.com
text:
BUCKHANNON, W.Va. — Children in Buckhannon will soon have new playground equipment thanks to a local donation.
The Stockert Youth and Community Center received a donation of just under $13,000 from Tim and Charlotte Critchfield on Thursday morning to purchase new playground equipment.
Lisa Lamb, director of the center, highlighted the impact of the contribution.
“This will upgrade the playground equipment that we already have,” she said. “We’re excited to add some new things to it.”
The funds were originally designated to help finance a new multipurpose building for the facility. When that project was canceled, the money was reallocated to support the playground, Tim Critchfield said.
“The Stockert Center does so much for the youth in the area,” he said. “We’re always glad to help when we can.”
In addition to the playground upgrades, the center has opened registration for its youth basketball program, which is open to children ages 5 to 14, Lamb said.
“A few city council members and a few other people have been helping to plan it,” she said. “We started registration (Thursday) and that will run through Nov. 17. We’ll be kicking off the season in December with three skills days and then starting games in January. It looks like it’s all coming together nicely.”
Between 200 and 300 children typically participate in the program each year, requiring careful coordination, Lamb said.
“There is a lot of planning and scheduling with different gyms,” she said. “We also have to get the coaches and kids organized.”
The program is a highlight for local children, Lamb said.
“They are excited to have something to do,” she said. “Especially if they don’t make the school teams, this is something else they can do for fun.”
Children of all skill levels and backgrounds are invited to participate, Lamb said.
“There are some kids who have never played before and they are learning these skills through this program,” she said. “This program might also be all that some kids have, so they are pretty excited to be a part of it.”
Lamb encouraged interested families to reach out to the center for more information or volunteer.
“Parents can always call us for more information,” she said. “They are also more than welcome to help with things like the scoreboard.”
